title: An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge
focus: the mind's final escape at the moment of death

teacherSummary.text: Peyton Farquhar, a Southern planter, stands on a railroad bridge in Alabama about to be hanged by Union soldiers. Part II flashes back: a disguised Union scout tempted him to try burning the bridge. In Part III the rope seems to break; he swims, dodges bullets, and walks all night to his home, where his wife waits. As he reaches for her, a blow falls: he is dead, his body swinging beneath the bridge.

context.history: Bierce fought for the Union at Shiloh and Chickamauga; the story (1890) is in Tales of Soldiers and Civilians.

significance: A celebrated experiment with time and point of view; the twist depends on shifting from objective to subjective narration.
